name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.128.0 — CLIENT replaces SIGNOFF as the last human gate of /spec:mocks: the driver derives CLIENT where it derived SIGNOFF, `client open --address <url>` records an exposed serve after probing `<url>/client/__notes/list` over http or https, and design-atlas.js serve grows a /client route whose writes stamp a note's origin from the route it arrived on rather than the typed name. A client's mock-scope note captures its anchored screen at raise through lib/client-capture.js (the look command's own URL form and first-declared viewport, sha256 on the note); `notes address --port <n>` re-captures and refuses an unchanged hash, so a fix is recorded only on a visible change. Only the client route resolves a client note — withdrawn from open, accepted from addressed — and a session-route resolve is a 403. `notes waive --id --reason` releases a client note or a question after seven days of client silence, marking a question's ledger row `waived <date>`, and `--mark approved` prints the waived count and every reason. writeNotes becomes a tmp-file rename so two writers can never tear notes.json. 7.127.0 — The review driver's second and later reviewer passes now review the fix, not the whole range again: at each reviewer return the driver snapshots the working tree as a git tree object through a scratch index (untracked files included, the real index and worktree untouched), and at fix-applied it diffs that snapshot against a fresh one to write the iteration's changed-file list into the sidecar. A fix that changed no file is refused before any legs run, saving a whole legs run and reviewer dispatch. The iteration-2+ REVIEWER step is a fix-delta pass that hands the reviewer that list plus the prior reviewer and disposer returns, and the reviewer agent's contract narrows to re-verifying fix-routed findings and reporting only inside the listed files. 7.126.0 — Soft reviewer findings are now advisory: verdict.js's disposition pool holds only hard survivors plus leg findings, so a soft-only reviewer return derives CLEAN with zero dispositions instead of demanding a fix/waive/reject cycle, and the review row carries the soft count as an eighth findings key. FINDINGS keeps exactly one meaning, a dispatched fix that has not landed. The review driver self-dispositions an empty hard pool straight to CLOSE with no DISPOSITIONS mark required, prints soft survivors once under an advisory block that is never routed to the disposer, and --mark dispositions --file now derives the waived/rejected/fix-dispatched tallies from the disposer return itself, with the count flags becoming an optional cross-check rather than a hand-typed requirement. reviewer.md's severity calibration drops the medium level: hard blocks CLEAN until dispositioned, soft is advisory.
